transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. Like, I'll worry about leaving my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or... or maybe not setting up my classroom materials safely. And the thing is, even when I know I probably handled it just fine, the doubt just keeps popping back into my head. It's just been really bothering me lately.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to get rid of these nagging thoughts?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I leave the house or my classroom, I usually end up going back over the same things a few times. I'll check my aunt's pill organizer, make sure the stove is off, or look over my lesson plans again. Sometimes I just silently replay what I just did in my head to make sure I didn't mess anything up. 

I basically just keep checking until I feel calm enough to actually walk out the door. It's frustrating because it definitely makes me run late sometimes, but I just feel like I have to do it to move on.
Do you feel anxious when you have these nagging thoughts?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. Um, it's mostly just this... really unsettled feeling. I don't know if I'd call it full-blown anxiety, but it's like I just can't relax or focus on whatever I'm supposed to be doing until I go back and check. So, yeah, it definitely makes me feel on edge.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that aren't related to your concerns about forgetting something or making a mistake?

No, not really. It's pretty much just the stuff I mentioned—worrying I forgot to do something or didn't do it right, like with my aunt's medicine or my classroom stuff. I don't really have any other weird thoughts or urges besides that.
Do you feel like checking these things over and over helps reduce your unsettled feeling?

Yeah, it does. Um, like I mentioned earlier, going back over those same things a few times—checking the stove, my aunt's pill organizer, or just silently replaying what I did in my head—it's really the only way I can get that unsettled feeling to go away. I basically just have to keep doing it until I feel calm enough to move on and actually leave the house or my classroom. So it does help, even though, you know, it makes me run late sometimes.
Are these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors affecting your relationships or work performance?

I mean, I'm still getting through my work and family commitments fine. I haven't dropped the ball on anything major. But... my mornings definitely take longer now. Because of all the checking, I sometimes arrive at school feeling really rushed, or like I'm already behind before the day even starts. 

And it kind of affects my downtime, too. Like, my lesson prep for my classes, or even just my evening journaling—they just don't feel as smooth or as restorative as they used to. It just takes more out of me now.
Do you feel like these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are significantly interfering with your overall quality of life?

I guess, um, like I was just saying, it's not completely stopping me from living my life. I'm still getting through all my work and family commitments. But it's definitely a drag. 

Because my mornings take so much longer now, getting to school feeling rushed and already behind is really frustrating. And then later on, my lesson prep and my evening journaling just... they don't feel as smooth or restorative anymore. So, it is interfering, but I'm still managing to get by.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind even when you try to ignore them?

Yeah, I do. That's actually the main reason I decided to come in. I just keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something really important. Like, I'll worry that I left my aunt's medicine out wrong, or that I didn't set up my classroom materials safely for the kids. And I'll try to just push the thought away, because logically I know I probably handled it fine, but... the doubt just keeps popping right back into my head anyway.
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors beyond checking things, in order to relieve your nagging thoughts?

Not really anything beyond the checking, no. It's mostly just... before I leave the house or my classroom, I'll go back over the same things a few times. I'll check my aunt's pill organizer, make sure the stove is off, look over my lesson plans again. Or sometimes I'll just silently replay what I did in my head to make sure I did it right. I just keep doing that until I feel calm enough to actually leave and move on. That's what ends up making me run late sometimes. But it's really just the checking and replaying, not any other specific rituals.
Do you have thoughts that are disturbing or unpleasant to you, beyond just the worry about forgetting something?

No, not really. It's really just the worrying that I forgot to do something important or didn't do it right. I don't have any other kinds of disturbing thoughts, just the constant doubting about my responsibilities.
Do you feel like these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of distress?

Well, it's definitely frustrating, but I wouldn't say it's completely overwhelming. I'm still getting through work and taking care of my aunt just fine. It's just... my mornings take a lot longer than they should. I end up arriving at school feeling rushed and already behind before the kids even get there. And things I used to enjoy, like prepping my lessons or just doing my evening journaling, they don't feel as relaxing or smooth as they used to because I'm just double-checking everything in my head. So it's bothersome, definitely, but I'm still functioning.
Do you feel like these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are a part of who you are, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

I mean, they definitely feel like my own thoughts. It's not like a voice in my head or anything coming from outside. It's just me, worrying about my own stuff—my aunt, my classroom, my house. It just feels like my normal worrying, just... turned up a lot louder than it used to be. But yeah, it's definitely just me.
Do you often feel anxious in situations that don't involve your nagging thoughts about forgetting something?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel anxious just in general. If I'm not worrying about whether I locked the door or turned off the stove, I feel pretty normal. It's really just tied to those specific things I feel responsible for. Outside of that, I'm not a particularly anxious person.
Do you often feel anxious when you're not thinking about your responsibilities or potential mistakes?

Like I was just saying, no, not really. Um, if I'm not actively thinking about my responsibilities—like my classroom or taking care of my aunt—I feel completely fine. I don't just sit around feeling nervous for no reason. It really only hits me when I'm worried I've made a mistake with those specific things.
Would you say that these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you significant distress?

I wouldn't say it's severe, but it is definitely frustrating. I'm still getting through all my work and family commitments just fine. But, um, my mornings definitely take a lot longer now. Sometimes I arrive at school feeling really rushed, like I'm already behind before the day even starts. 

And then later on, doing my lesson prep or just trying to do my evening journaling... it just doesn't feel as smooth or as restorative as it used to. So, it's definitely getting in the way and causing some stress, even if I'm still managing to get everything done.
Are you having difficulty meeting your responsibilities at work or at home because of these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors?

Well, like I mentioned a moment ago, no, I'm not actually dropping the ball on anything. I'm still getting through all my work and family commitments just fine. It's really just that the process is harder now. 

Because my mornings take so much longer, I sometimes get to school feeling really rushed and behind before the day even starts. And then later, when I'm doing my lesson prep, or even just trying to do my evening journaling, it just doesn't feel as smooth or as restorative as it used to. So I am meeting my responsibilities, it's just... taking a lot more out of me to get it all done.
Do you often worry about things in general, not just the specific things like forgetting your aunt's medicine or classroom materials?

No, not really. Um, I think I mentioned it a bit earlier, but I don't really consider myself a worrier in general. If it's not about my aunt's medication or making sure my classroom is set up right, I'm usually pretty relaxed. I don't really stress about everyday stuff outside of those specific responsibilities.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy social activities or spend time with family and friends because of these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors?

Well, like I was saying before, I'm still getting through my family commitments and everything just fine. I wouldn't say it's stopping me from seeing people or anything like that. It's really just the time it takes up, you know? My mornings take a lot longer now, and I end up getting to school feeling rushed. And then in the evenings, doing my lesson prep or my journaling, it just doesn't feel as smooth or restorative. So I'm still doing all the things I usually do, it's just... it just takes more out of me.
Do you have any repetitive behaviors or mental acts that you feel driven to perform, outside of checking things related to your responsibilities?

No, not really. It's just the checking I've already talked about, like with the medicine and the classroom stuff. I don't have any other rituals or things like that I feel like I have to do. It's pretty much just focused on making sure I didn't mess up those specific things.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with your aunt or other family members because of these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors?

Yeah, I think I actually just touched on that a second ago. Um, no, I'm still getting through my family commitments and spending time with my aunt just fine. It hasn't really ruined that for me. 

It's really just... like I said, it's the time it takes up. My mornings just take a lot longer now, and I sometimes arrive at school feeling rushed or already behind before the day even starts. And then later on, doing my lesson prep or my evening journaling, it just doesn't feel as smooth or restorative as it used to. But the actual time I spend with my family is still okay.
